M1_prevent_reflux.mechanism: Mechanical one-way valve + geometric flow restrictor at venous boundary
M1_prevent_reflux.how_it_breaks_loop: Eliminates blood entry → no thrombus substrate → no feedback
M1_prevent_reflux.causal_leverage: HIGHEST — removes the root cause (blood entering shunt)
M1_prevent_reflux.heparin_comparison: Does not need heparin — prevents blood entry entirely
M1_prevent_reflux.architectural_reason: eShunt venous boundary REQUIRES a one-way mechanism — ventricular catheters don't face venous pressure

M2_prevent_thrombus_initiation.intervention_point: P2 — prevent thrombus initiation (prevent clot from blood that enters)
M2_prevent_thrombus_initiation.mechanism: Heparin-eluting coating at venous boundary zone (dual-zone: anti-fouling CSF side + anti-thrombogenic venous side)
M2_prevent_thrombus_initiation.how_it_breaks_loop: Blood enters but cannot form thrombus → no obstruction → no stasis
M2_prevent_thrombus_initiation.causal_leverage: HIGH — prevents the second step of the feedback loop
risks: Heparin elution is FINITE — depletes over time
M2_prevent_thrombus_initiation.heparin_comparison: THIS IS the heparin branch — must stress-test whether it delays or prevents thrombosis
M2_prevent_thrombus_initiation.architectural_reason: Dual-zone coating is eShunt-specific — venous boundary creates blood contact zone that ventricular catheters don't have

M3_prevent_thrombus_propagation.intervention_point: P3 — prevent thrombus propagation (stop clot growth)
M3_prevent_thrombus_propagation.mechanism: Surface nanostructure that prevents fibrin network formation (prevents clot propagation, not initiation)
M3_prevent_thrombus_propagation.how_it_breaks_loop: Thrombus initiates but cannot grow → micro-clots don't accumulate → no obstruction
M3_prevent_thrombus_propagation.causal_leverage: MEDIUM — allows initiation but blocks propagation
M3_prevent_thrombus_propagation.heparin_comparison: Different mechanism — not drug-eluting, surface physics
M3_prevent_thrombus_propagation.architectural_reason: Propagation prevention via surface nanostructure is a general biomaterials concept, not eShunt-specific

M4_active_clearing.intervention_point: P4 — actively clear thrombus (remove existing clot)
M4_active_clearing.mechanism: Periodic micro-pump reverse-flow flush cycle that dislodges deposits
M4_active_clearing.how_it_breaks_loop: Accumulated thrombus is periodically removed → prevents saturation
M4_active_clearing.causal_leverage: MEDIUM — treats symptom, not cause; but can reset state
M4_active_clearing.heparin_comparison: Active vs passive — doesn't prevent thrombus but removes it
M4_active_clearing.architectural_reason: Active clearing requires a pump — only eShunt with micro-pump can do this

M5_maintain_flow_despite_thrombus.intervention_point: P5 — maintain flow despite thrombus (geometry/pump overcomes obstruction)
M5_maintain_flow_despite_thrombus.mechanism: Shunt geometry with redundant flow paths + pressure-adaptive lumen that maintains drainage even with partial obstruction
M5_maintain_flow_despite_thrombus.how_it_breaks_loop: Obstruction doesn't cause stasis → no positive feedback → thrombus doesn't accelerate
M5_maintain_flow_despite_thrombus.causal_leverage: MEDIUM — breaks the stasis→thrombus link in the feedback loop
risks: May not prevent eventual full occlusion
M5_maintain_flow_despite_thrombus.heparin_comparison: Doesn't prevent thrombus at all — just maintains drainage
M5_maintain_flow_despite_thrombus.architectural_reason: Redundant flow paths are a general design principle, not eShunt-specific

M6_combined_P1_P2.intervention_point: P1+P2 — prevent reflux AND prevent thrombus initiation
M6_combined_P1_P2.mechanism: Mechanical one-way valve (P1) + heparin-eluting venous zone (P2) — belt and suspenders
M6_combined_P1_P2.how_it_breaks_loop: Eliminates blood entry (P1) AND prevents thrombus from any blood that does enter (P2)
M6_combined_P1_P2.causal_leverage: HIGHEST — dual intervention at two points
M6_combined_P1_P2.heparin_comparison: Combines heparin with mechanical prevention — heparin is backup, not primary
M6_combined_P1_P2.architectural_reason: eShunt venous boundary is the ONLY shunt type that needs both reflux prevention AND anti-thrombogenic coating

verdict.conclusion: Heparin MERELY DELAYS thrombosis at all tested half-lives. Even with 365-day half-life, heparin effectiveness drops to ~63% at 365 days, and obstruction still reaches saturation. Heparin does NOT genuinely change long-horizon patency — it only delays. M2 (heparin-eluting) is INSUFFICIENT as a standalone F4 solution.
